purpose: Authoritative sequencing for the georeferencing delivery and reusable data-product work.
current_phase_gate: Phase 13 is defined on an isolated branch with a clean merged-main baseline; human approval is required before UI implementation.
phase_gate_policy: A planned phase is not approved for implementation until its scope, isolated branch, approved baseline, allowed paths, verification commands, and human approval are recorded in current_phase.json.

phases.name: Country ETL and HITL review automation
phases.objective: Turn country evaluation into a deterministic ETL and review pipeline, define approved build profiles for the 21 unevaluated countries, and run the 21-country expansion with reproducible evidence and HITL review.
required_validation: The five existing country outcomes are reproduced without changing their artifacts or classifications.
The 21 unevaluated countries receive approved profiles and an ETL result or an explicit unavailable/not_evaluated outcome.
The 21-country report records 4 verified, 7 partial, and 10 unavailable outcomes, with 17 published artifacts and 4 withheld outcomes.
Automated checks distinguish routine pass, review required, and blocked outcomes.
Missing qualifying source objects remain target-level not_evaluated.
No production write, runtime scraping, database migration, or delivery-architecture change is introduced.

phases.name: Recovery calibration and real-world benchmarking
exit_requirements: Run and record country-level benchmark evidence for Guyana, Belize, and Jamaica.
Complete the Phase 7 walkthrough, including scope, baseline comparison, verification, risks, rollback, and unresolved human decisions.
Keep benchmark results distinct from surveyed accuracy claims and preserve explicit partial or unavailable outcomes.

phases.name: Reference artifact architecture and delivery
phases.objective: Establish immutable artifact manifests, GCS/CDN delivery and caching, versioned URLs, integrity checks, and a packaged offline fallback.

phases.name: GeoParquet reusable data-product foundation
phases.objective: Define and validate the canonical GeoParquet artifact for reusable geospatial and AI workflows, including schema, geometry encoding, CRS, precision, attributes, provenance, country partitioning, deterministic builds, hashes, and interoperability.
phases.delivery_contract: Use the canonical data product for downstream reuse; choose the browser delivery representation through a measured bakeoff. PMTiles/MVT may be a derived display artifact and GeoJSON may remain a debug/export representation rather than the canonical store.
required_validation: Compare GeoParquet with FlatGeobuf and PMTiles/MVT for size, build cost, access pattern, and operational complexity.
Exercise the same artifact path intended for production Recovery matching and browser display.
Verify Python, R, and browser interoperability without forcing the browser to parse the canonical artifact if a derived display artifact is superior.
must_not_include: Database migrations unless separately approved by evidence
Recovery algorithm replacement unless Phase 7 evidence requires it

phases.name: Caribbean country coverage batch
phases.objective: Build and benchmark bounded Caribbean country increments using the established artifact, GeoParquet, and provenance contracts; weak countries may remain partial or unavailable.
scope_notes: Use small independently reviewable country increments rather than an all-or-nothing regional release.
Record country-level benchmark outcomes as verified, partial, or unavailable; do not represent source-name agreement as surveyed accuracy.
Do not commit raw source geospatial datasets or add runtime scraping.
Phase 9 does not change the canonical GeoParquet schema or delivery architecture; defects in those foundations require a separately approved scope update.
exit_requirements: Each selected Caribbean country has a bounded profile, provenance record, deterministic artifact manifest, and benchmark result.
Country outcomes and limitations are documented without blocking on weak or unavailable countries.
All scoped tests pass against the approved baseline and a Phase 9 walkthrough records rollback and unresolved risks.

phases.name: Central American country coverage batch
phases.objective: Build and benchmark bounded Central American country increments using the established artifact, GeoParquet, and provenance contracts; weak countries may remain partial or unavailable.
scope_notes: Begin with a bounded Costa Rica increment; later Central American countries require the same independent review and remain separate internal slices.
Belize is already covered by Phase 9 and is not reworked in this phase.
Do not commit raw source geospatial datasets, add runtime scraping, alter the canonical GeoParquet schema, or change delivery architecture.
exit_requirements: Each selected Central American country has a bounded profile, provenance record, deterministic artifact manifest, and benchmark result.
Country outcomes and limitations are documented as verified, partial, or unavailable.
All scoped tests pass against the approved baseline and a Phase 10 walkthrough records rollback and unresolved risks.

phases.name: South American country coverage batch
phases.objective: Build and benchmark bounded South American country increments using the established artifact, GeoParquet, and provenance contracts; weak countries may remain partial or unavailable.
scope_notes: Begin with a bounded Suriname increment; remaining countries require separate internal slices.
Guyana is already covered and is not reworked in this phase.
Do not commit raw source geospatial datasets, add runtime scraping, alter the canonical GeoParquet schema, or change delivery architecture.
exit_requirements: Each selected South American country has a bounded profile, provenance record, deterministic artifact manifest, and benchmark result.
Country outcomes and limitations are documented as verified, partial, or unavailable.
All scoped tests pass against the approved baseline and a Phase 11 walkthrough records rollback and unresolved risks.

phases.name: Georeferencer UI/UX polish
phases.objective: Improve the Georeferencer page's visual hierarchy, progressive task flow, result evidence presentation, map inspection controls, accessibility, and responsive behavior without changing georeferencing semantics or API contracts.
exit_requirements: Focused browser evidence covers primary upload, error/loading, result, and map-inspection flows.
Existing backend, TypeScript, and frontend lint verification passes.
Responsive and accessible interaction behavior is documented in a walkthrough.
A human-reviewed PR records rollback and unresolved design decisions.

phases.name: Georeferencing program closeout
phases.objective: Confirm the final supported-country inventory, artifact manifests and hashes, benchmark evidence, known limitations, operational fallback, documentation, and rollback procedures.

conditional_follow_ons.name: Field or surveyed accuracy validation
conditional_follow_ons.trigger: Only if a separately approved accuracy objective and independent control data are established.

conditional_follow_ons.name: Recovery algorithm improvement
conditional_follow_ons.trigger: Only if benchmark evidence demonstrates a production-relevant failure that the current algorithm cannot address.

conditional_follow_ons.name: Database or schema migration
conditional_follow_ons.trigger: Only if the artifact/delivery design proves a migration is necessary; it requires its own explicit approval and rollback plan.

permanent_exclusions: Runtime Nominatim or other live scraping
Representing source-name agreement as surveyed positional accuracy
